He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Independence Community College|Independence CC Pirates]], the [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College|Northeastern Oklahoma A&M Golden Norsemen]], the [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State Bears]], and the [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco Dons]]. ==Early life and high school career== Mogbo grew up in [[West Palm Beach, Florida]] and attended [[Forest Hill Community High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/11/27/hs-boys-basketball-forest-hill-puts-on-show-in-win-over-hallandale/2203382007/|title=HS boys basketball: Forest Hill puts on a show in win over Hallandale|work=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|date=November 27, 2019|access-date=May 30, 2024}} ==College career== Mogbo had no Division I scholarship offers in high school began his college basketball career at [[Independence Community College]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/jonathan-mogbo-flourishes-usf-fifth-school-5-18705974.php|title=Jonathan Mogbo flourishes at USF, fifth school in 5 years, 5 states|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|access-date=May 29, 2024}} He transferred to [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College]] before the start of his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/jan/24/key-matchup-usfs-jonathan-mogbo-gonzagas-anton-wat/|title=Key matchup: USF's Jonathan Mogbo, Gonzaga's Anton Watson have similar roles|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=January 24, 2024|access-date=May 29, 2024}} Magbo averaged 14.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks per game with the Golden Norsemen.{{cite web|url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/college/msu/2022/04/22/jonathan-mogbo-missouri-state-basketball-juco-transfer-dana-ford-northeastern-oklahoma-neo/7412497001/|title=Jonathan Mogbo: Missouri State basketball adds juco transfer|work=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|date=April 22, 2022|access-date=May 30, 2024}} Mogbo transferred to [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State]] for his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/basketball/west-coast-conference-transfer-portal-update-gonzaga-santa-clara-lmu-reload-for-2023-24|title=West Coast Conference transfer portal update: Gonzaga, Santa Clara, LMU reload for 2023-24|first=Cole|last=Forsman|website=[[SI.com]]|date=August 23, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}} He was the Bears' starting power forward and averaged eight points, seven rebounds, 1.4 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. After the season, Mogbo entered NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/college/msu/2023/03/14/jonathan-mogbo-transfer-portal-missouri-state-northeastern-oklahoma-am-college-basketaball/70009954007/|title=Missouri State basketball starter Jonathan Mogbo enters transfer portal|first=Wyatt D.|last=Wheeler|work=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}} Mogbo ultimately transferred to [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/nil-basketball-bay-area-recruiting-18472265.php|title=How NIL upends Bay Area schools' basketball recruiting|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=November 24, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://usfdons.com/news/2023/4/25/mens-basketball-usf-adds-dynamic-forward-jonathan-mogbo.aspx|title=USF Adds Dynamic Forward Jonathan Mogbo|website=USFDons.com|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}} He was named the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) Newcomer of the Year and first-team All-WCC after averaging 14.2 points and a conference-high 10.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/college/gonzaga-and-brigham-young-will-rule-the-west-in-mens-basketball-next-season/|title=Gonzaga and Brigham Young will rule the West in men's basketball next season|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=April 11, 2024|access-date=May 30, 2024}} After the season, Mogbo declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] and re-entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]]. He opted to remain in the draft and forgo his remaining season of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2024/05/28/san-francisco-jonathan-mogbo-2024-nba-draft/|title=Report: San Francisco junior Jonathan Mogbo to remain in 2024 NBA
